samuel2.11.p1.b1.text: In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, David sent out Joab and his servants with the whole army of Israel.

samuel2.11.p1.b3.text: One evening David got up from his bed and strolled around on the roof of the palace. And from the roof he saw a woman bathing—a very beautiful woman.

samuel2.11.p2.b1.text: “This is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”

samuel2.11.p2.b2.text: Then David sent messengers to get her, …

samuel2.11.p2.b3.text: … she came to him, … Then she returned home.

samuel2.11.p2.b4.text: And the woman conceived and sent word to David, saying, “I am pregnant.”

samuel2.11.p3.b2.text: “Go down to your house and wash your feet.”

samuel2.11.p3.b3.text: So Uriah left the palace, and a gift from the king followed him.

samuel2.11.p3.b4.text: But Uriah slept at the door of the palace with all his master’s servants; he did not go down to his house.

samuel2.11.p4.b1.text: “Haven’t you just arrived from a journey?” David asked Uriah. “Why didn’t you go home?”

samuel2.11.p4.b2.text: “The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in tents, … How can I go to my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? As surely as you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing!”

samuel2.11.p4.b3.text: Then David invited Uriah to eat and drink with him, and he got Uriah drunk.

samuel2.11.p4.b4.text: And in the evening Uriah went out to lie down on his cot with his master’s servants, but he did not go home.

samuel2.11.p5.b1.text: The next morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.

samuel2.11.p5.b2.text: In the letter he wrote: “Put Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle; then withdraw from him, so that he may be struck down and killed.”

samuel2.11.p6.b1.text: So as Joab besieged the city, he assigned Uriah to a place where he saw the strongest enemy soldiers.

samuel2.11.p6.b2.text: And when the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of David’s servants fell, …

samuel2.11.p6.b3.text: … and Uriah the Hittite also died.

samuel2.11.p7.b1.text: Joab sent to David a full account of the battle

samuel2.11.p7.b2.text: if the king’s anger flares, he may ask you, ‘Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Did you not realize they would shoot from atop the wall?

samuel2.11.p7.b3.text: … Was it not a woman who dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? …

samuel2.11.p7.b4.text: If so, then you are to say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.’

samuel2.11.p8.b1.text: So the messenger set out and reported to David all that Joab had sent him to say.

samuel2.11.p8.b2.text: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king’s servants were killed. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.”

samuel2.11.p8.b3.text: “Say this to Joab: ‘Do not let this matter upset you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Strengthen your attack against the city and demolish it.’

samuel2.11.p9.b1.text: When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.

samuel2.11.p9.b2.text: And when the time of mourning was over, David had her brought to his house, and she became his wife …

samuel2.11.p9.b4.text: But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.
